chapter: Arrangers, Bill Robinson and Coleman Hawkins
title: Interludes from Jelly Roll and writing for his own record dates
summary: Thomas credits Jelly for his use of interludes, tailors progressions to Jonah Jones and Charlie Shavers, and recalls the first solo he took on a record.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I wrote certain things when I wrote my arrangements that I wrote for Ben, and he'd play them so beautiful. I wrote... I had another knack. I got this from Jelly Roll. I've got to give Jelly Roll credit. He used to always have interludes...
Little things. And I've had more interludes in my (?) own arrangements... They didn't mean nothin' but a

tune. But it's just something refreshing to go from one chorus to another. And I used to do a little trickeration thing. I wrote... Like, I knew how Jonah Jones played, so I wrote certain progressions for him. And I did the same thing for Charlie Shavers. Because Charlie Shavers had a thing I remember he played with that little small band.
Oh, you did that on your record date.
Yeah, on my record date. And that's why... The reason my record dates were so great was because of the kind of musicians I had.

I recorded a lot with Cozy when he was recording. And I used to write the arrangements, and I'd be up there rehearsing the band and everything... And one day, I finally played a solo. I hadn't played... Milt, I had such great musicians... What the heck was I doing playing solos when I'd have Coleman Hawkins and Ben Webster... Those guys could play better solos than I, and I knew it! So I wrote the arrangements to feature my men.

So one day I think I had arrangements for I think it was Cozy, and I played a solo. And the guys in the control room came out and said, 'it's about time.' Because see, they had never heard me play a solo. I was just making arrangements. And then finally, one day, I made a solo, and
they said, "It's about time." I think they was glad to see me do something. I just played some of the little short parts.
